bodyHtml:
Use this guide to decide whether OpenBrowser belongs on your shortlist: start with its stated purpose, then check setup, activity signals, maintenance clues, and adoption risks.

What is OpenBrowser?

本地指纹浏览器 · 多环境隔离 · 代理 / 指纹 / 同步 / RPA

Evidence: github.com

Who should consider it?

This guide is most relevant to frontend developers evaluating tools in the JavaScript ecosystem. The source associates the project with chromium, electron, fingerprint browser, proxy. Treat it as a starting point for a shortlist, then compare the official documentation with your own requirements.

Evidence: github.com

Why is it getting attention?

The repository appeared in this feed because its recorded GitHub activity made it notable at collection time. Stars and forks indicate attention, not technical quality, security, or suitability.

At collection time, the official source recorded 255 GitHub stars, 58 forks, 1 open issues, and a last recorded source push on 2026-07-23.

Evidence: api.github.com

How to evaluate it

Open the official repository before trying OpenBrowser. Review its README, recent releases, issue tracker, security policy, and license, then test it in a non-production project that matches your environment.

Treat stars, forks, and issue counts as repository signals rather than proof of quality, security, maintenance, or suitability. Review documentation, releases, issues, security policy, and license.

Evidence: github.com, api.github.com

Bottom line

OpenBrowser has enough public source information to warrant a closer look, but the available activity signals are not a recommendation. The useful next step is to verify fit against the official documentation and test the project for your own constraints.
